key_insight: Tanner-graph spectral reduction lets routing and syndrome-extraction depth for HGP/LP and BB qLDPC codes be analyzed with much smaller algebraic objects, enabling faster design of multi-layer optical lattice routing.
engineering_relevance: This work suggests a practical path to lower per-cycle routing overhead in 3D reconfigurable quantum hardware by stacking AOL layers and reducing atom motion during repeated syndrome extraction.
method: Reduce HGP/LP Tanner analysis to a single SVD on the base parity-check matrix and use the relation β_HGP = (1 + β_base)/2.
Use Fourier character decomposition for BB codes so the Tanner spectrum becomes lm independent 2×2 SVDs instead of one large diagonalization.
Map the resulting spectral/routing structure into a multi-layer AOL protocol with amortized Valiant-style setup and per-cycle layer scheduling.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports exact spectral identities, an 8× step-count reduction at L_layers ≥ 8, and estimated ~50–300× wall-clock speedup versus a single-layer AOD baseline.
watch_item: The projected gains depend on multi-layer AOL hardware assumptions and could shrink substantially with crosstalk or if only a single layer is available.
paper_title: Using Tanner Spectral Reduction to Improve Multi-Layer Optical Lattice Routing for Hypergraph-Product and Bivariate Bicycle qLDPC Codes
